full_judgment:
7. Mr. Md. Shah Alam, learned Advocate appearing for the appellants assail the judgment particularly on the ground that Other Class Suit having been filed prior to the kabala of these plaintiffs and common vendor of the plaintiffs, defendant No. 1 contested the earlier suit by filing written statement the transaction made in favour of the plaintiffs is hit by section 52 of Transfer of Property Act. Learned Advocate submits that, during continuation of the suit if there be any change made by any parties by transfer, the purchaser will be bound by the result of the suit. Learned Advocate on refenence to the plaint, submits that, from the plaint it appears that plaintiff admitted that bainapatra was executed on 9-9-1985 and defendant No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 246 of 1987 on 19-6-1987 and the plaintiffs admitted that they have purchased the suit land in December, 1987 as such all transactions is hit by principal of lispendency. Learned Advocate relied on the decisions of KM Zahirul Haque vs	Shahida	Khanam, 12 BLC (AD) 65, the case of Jamaluddin vs Rabeya Begum, 32 DLR 63, the case of Muzaffor Ali vs Messrs Monwora Hospital, 19 BLD 484 = 51 DLR 341, the case of Hochenaddi Shaikh vs Esrnail Sikder, 9 DLR 294, the case of Debendra Chandra Saha, decree-holder vs Nabin alias Nalini Chandra Pal, 7 DLR 186. 

 8. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Advocate, appearing for the plaintiff-respondents, on the other hand, submits that, in the instant case the question calls for determination as to whose documents executed earlier. Learned Advocate further submits that, it is not denied that the deed of the plaintiffs were later in point of time than the bainama of the defendant No. 1 but the kabalas of the plaintiffs executed much earlier than the kabala of the defendant No. 1 which was executed in 1997 and on reference to section 47 of the Registration Act, submits that, section 47 of the Registration Act provides when there is conflict in between the parties as to their purchase from the same vendor the question of title to be acquired by the person whose deed was executed earlier and submits that since the deed of the plaintiffs being earlier in point of time before the kabala of the defendant No. 1 executed through Court and by this time the suit property transferred to the plaintiffs and after kabalas, plaintiffs mutated their names, paying rents and taxes and also constructed pucca and semi pucca structures on the suit land, as such deed in favour of the plaintiffs acted upon, as such the decree passed by the learned judge should not be interfere. Learned Advocate in support of his submission relied on the decision of Secretary, Board of Trustee, RAJLIK Karmachari Kalyan Trust vs Dhaka City Corporation and others, 2 MLR (AD) 101, the case of Abdur Rashid vs Abdul Bashir, 20 BLD (AD) 262 = 5 BLC (AD) 185, the case of Mir Abdul Ali vs Md Rafiqul Islam, 8 BLD (AD)149 = 40 DLR (AD) 75, the case of Haji Md Ishaque vs Rupali Bank, 43 DLR 621. 

 14. Section 47 of the Registration Act as we see is that if there be any conflict in between two parties of the same property transferred by same vendor then the deed in favour of person executed earlier will prevail over the other deed, when the deed registered then it will take effect from the date when it was executed. In the case of Azizuddin vs Abu Taleb Sarder, 35 DLR 360, where the Court found the defendant's kabala was executed earlier than the plaintiffs kabala which though executed later was, however, registered before the defendant's kabala; it was held that execution of the defendant's Kabala being earlier in point of time will have precedence over the plaintiff's kabala. 

 15. Mr Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Advocate, on section 47 of the Registration Act relied on the case of Mir Abdul Ali vs Md Rafiqul Islam, 8 BLD (AD)149 = 40 DLR (AD) 75, where the question was when there be successive documents of transfer by self-same vendor, question as to which document is valid and it was decided that 'a document that has been registered relates back to the date of its execution. The question of title as between the two contestants claiming on the basis of successive documents executed by the self-same vendor must be determined with reference to the title to the later on the date of execution and not of registration'. Other decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff respondent were of the same line.
